<!-- page: api/SharpCell.CellBorderStyle.md -->

# CellBorderStyle

```csharp
public enum CellBorderStyle
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

The lines Excel draws borders with.

## Values

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="thin"></a>`Thin` | 0 | A thin solid line. |
| <a id="medium"></a>`Medium` | 1 | A solid line of medium weight. |
| <a id="thick"></a>`Thick` | 2 | A thick solid line. |
| <a id="double"></a>`Double` | 3 | Two thin lines. |
| <a id="hair"></a>`Hair` | 4 | A hairline, thinner than [CellBorderStyle.Thin](SharpCell.CellBorderStyle.md#thin). |
| <a id="dotted"></a>`Dotted` | 5 | A thin line of dots. |
| <a id="dashed"></a>`Dashed` | 6 | A thin dashed line. |
| <a id="dashdot"></a>`DashDot` | 7 | A thin line of dashes and dots. |
| <a id="dashdotdot"></a>`DashDotDot` | 8 | A thin line of a dash and two dots. |
| <a id="mediumdashed"></a>`MediumDashed` | 9 | A dashed line of medium weight. |
| <a id="mediumdashdot"></a>`MediumDashDot` | 10 | A line of dashes and dots of medium weight. |
| <a id="mediumdashdotdot"></a>`MediumDashDotDot` | 11 | A line of a dash and two dots of medium weight. |
| <a id="slantdashdot"></a>`SlantDashDot` | 12 | A slanted line of dashes and dots of medium weight. |

|---|---|---|
| <a id="general"></a>`General` | 0 | Excel's default: numbers right, text left, logical values and errors in the middle. |

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.CellRange.md -->

# CellRange

```csharp
public sealed class CellRange
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

A rectangle of cells on one sheet, such as `A1:C10`. Like a [Cell](SharpCell.Cell.md), it is a handle: creating one allocates no cells.

## Properties

<a id="address"></a>
### Address

```csharp
public string Address { get; }
```

The A1 address without the sheet name: `A1:C10`, or `B2` for one cell.

<a id="cells"></a>
### Cells

```csharp
public IEnumerable<Cell> Cells { get; }
```

The cells of the range that hold something (a constant, a formula or a value spilled into them), row by row and left to right. Only existing cells are visited, so `A:A` is cheap. Values and formulas of the cells may be changed while enumerating; adding or removing a cell of the sheet makes the next step throw `InvalidOperationException`.

<a id="firstcolumn"></a>
### FirstColumn

```csharp
public int FirstColumn { get; }
```

The first column, from 1 (A is 1).

<a id="firstrow"></a>
### FirstRow

```csharp
public int FirstRow { get; }
```

The first row, from 1.

<a id="lastcolumn"></a>
### LastColumn

```csharp
public int LastColumn { get; }
```

The last column, from 1.

<a id="lastrow"></a>
### LastRow

```csharp
public int LastRow { get; }
```

The last row, from 1.

<a id="worksheet"></a>
### Worksheet

```csharp
public Worksheet Worksheet { get; }
```

The sheet the range is on.

## Methods

<a id="copyto-cellrange"></a>
### CopyTo(CellRange)

```csharp
public CellRange CopyTo(CellRange destination)
```

Copies the range's cells to another range, as copying and pasting them in Excel does: values, formulas, number formats, styles, hyperlinks, notes, data validation and conditional formats. A formula's relative references keep their distance from its cell, so `=A1*2` in B1 becomes `=A2*2` in B2, and a reference that would point past the sheet's edge becomes `#REF!`. Empty cells of the range clear the cells they are copied to. When the destination is a whole number of times as tall and as wide as the range, the range repeats to fill it; otherwise it is copied once, with its top-left cell at the destination's. The cells are read before any is written, so the ranges may overlap. The destination can be in another workbook: formulas then refer to that workbook's sheets and names. A cell filled by a formula's spill is copied as its value, unless that formula is copied too and spills again. Data validation formulas keep their distance from each cell as cell formulas do. Merged cells, column widths and row heights are not copied. Every formula reading the cells written is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Parameters**

- `destination`: Where to copy the cells to.

**Returns:** The cells written to.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The copy would not fit on the sheet.
- `InvalidOperationException`: A cell written to is part of an array formula other than its top-left cell.
- `NotSupportedException`: The range holds part of an array formula (Ctrl+Shift+Enter), or a formula SharpCell cannot read (such as a link to another workbook), in a cell or a data validation rule, whose references could not be moved.

<a id="delete-deleteshift"></a>
### Delete(DeleteShift)

```csharp
public void Delete(DeleteShift shift)
```

Deletes the range's cells, as Excel's Delete with "Shift cells up" or "Shift cells left" does: the cells below (or to the right) in the range's columns (or rows) move into their place. A reference to a deleted cell becomes `#REF!`; otherwise references follow as with [CellRange.Insert](SharpCell.CellRange.md#insert-insertshift). A range of whole rows (or columns) deletes them.

**Parameters**

- `shift`: Which cells take the place of the deleted ones.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `shift` is not a defined value.
- `InvalidOperationException`: The cells that move would split a merged area, a table or an array formula, or a table would lose its header, totals or data rows.
- `NotSupportedException`: A formula on the sheet, or one naming it, cannot be read by SharpCell; or some of a table's columns would be deleted.

<a id="equals-cellrange"></a>
### Equals(CellRange)

```csharp
public bool Equals(CellRange? other)
```

Whether the other range is on the same sheet with the same corners.

<a id="equals-object"></a>
### Equals(object)

```csharp
public override bool Equals(object? obj)
```

Whether `obj` is a range on the same sheet with the same corners.

<a id="gethashcode"></a>
### GetHashCode()

```csharp
public override int GetHashCode()
```

A hash code consistent with [CellRange.Equals](SharpCell.CellRange.md#equals-cellrange).

<a id="getvalues"></a>
### GetValues()

```csharp
public CellValue[,] GetValues()
```

The value of every cell, empty ones included, indexed `[row, column]` from the range's top-left cell. A whole column allocates an element for each of its 1,048,576 cells; use [Worksheet.UsedRange](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#usedrange) or [CellRange.Cells](SharpCell.CellRange.md#cells) for sparse data.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidOperationException`: The range has more cells than an array can hold.

<a id="insert-insertshift"></a>
### Insert(InsertShift)

```csharp
public void Insert(InsertShift shift)
```

Inserts empty cells in place of the range, as Excel's Insert with "Shift cells down" or "Shift cells right" does: only the cells in the range's columns (or rows) move, along with their styles, number formats, hyperlinks, notes, data validation, merged areas and tables, and every reference to them follows. A reference to a range that only some of the moved cells are in stays as it was, as in Excel; data validation over such a range is split. A range of whole rows (or whole columns) inserts rows (or columns), as [Worksheet.InsertRows](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#insertrows-int-int) does. Every formula is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Parameters**

- `shift`: Where the cells beside the range go.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `shift` is not a defined value.
- `InvalidOperationException`: Content would be pushed off the sheet, or the cells that move would split a merged area, a table or an array formula.
- `NotSupportedException`: A formula on the sheet, or one naming it, cannot be read by SharpCell, so its references could not follow; or cells would be inserted inside a table's columns.

<a id="readrows-func-rangerow-t"></a>
### ReadRows<T>(Func<RangeRow, T>)

```csharp
public List<T> ReadRows<T>(Func<RangeRow, T> read)
```

Reads each row below the range's first row into an object, the first row naming the columns: `range.ReadRows(row => new Order(row["Region"].Text, row["Units"].Value.AsNumber()))`. The lambda picks the cells, so no reflection is needed. Whole columns such as `A:C` end at the last row used. Formulas out of date in the range are calculated first, so the cells hold their current values.

**Parameters**

- `read`: Makes an item from a row.

**Returns:** The items, in row order.

<a id="setvalues-cellvalue"></a>
### SetValues(CellValue[,])

```csharp
public void SetValues(CellValue[,] values)
```

Sets the value of every cell, as assigning [Cell.Value](SharpCell.Cell.md#value) would: formulas are replaced and [CellValue.Empty](SharpCell.CellValue.md#empty) clears a cell. Everything is checked before the first cell is written, so an exception leaves the sheet unchanged; a cell of an array formula other than its top-left cell is refused even when the range covers the whole array.

**Parameters**

- `values`: Values indexed `[row, column]`, exactly as large as the range.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The array's size differs from the range's, or it holds a Missing, array or lambda value.
- `InvalidOperationException`: A cell is part of an array formula other than its top-left cell.

<a id="sort-ireadonlylist-sortkey-bool-bool"></a>
### Sort(IReadOnlyList<SortKey>, bool, bool)

```csharp
public void Sort(IReadOnlyList<SortKey> keys, bool matchCase = false, bool leftToRight = false)
```

Sorts the rows of the range, or its columns, as Excel's Data > Sort does. Ascending, numbers come first, then text (ignoring case unless `matchCase`), then FALSE and TRUE, then errors, which are all equal; descending reverses that, and empty cells come last either way. Formulas out of date are calculated first.

The cells move with what they hold: values, formulas, number formats, styles, hyperlinks and notes. A moved formula's relative references keep their distance from its cell, as when it is copied, so `=B2*C2` moved to row 5 becomes `=B5*C5`; formulas elsewhere that point into the range are not changed, and read whatever was sorted into their cells. Data validation, conditional formats, row heights and hidden rows stay where they are. Every formula reading the cells is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Parameters**

- `keys`: The columns that order the rows (or the rows that order the columns), first key first.
- `matchCase`: Whether text of different case differs, lower case first, as Excel's Case sensitive option.
- `leftToRight`: Whether to sort the columns by rows, as Excel's Sort left to right option.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: A key's column (or row) is outside the range.
- `InvalidOperationException`: The range holds merged cells, or part of an array formula or a spill.
- `NotSupportedException`: The range holds a formula SharpCell cannot read (such as a link to another workbook).

<a id="sort-sortkey"></a>
### Sort(SortKey[])

```csharp
public void Sort(params SortKey[] keys)
```

Sorts the rows of the range, as Excel's Data > Sort does: by the first key's column, rows equal there by the second's, and so on; rows equal by every key keep their order. Without a key the first column orders the rows, ascending. See [CellRange.Sort](SharpCell.CellRange.md#sort-ireadonlylist-sortkey-bool-bool).

**Parameters**

- `keys`: The columns that order the rows.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: A key's column is outside the range.
- `InvalidOperationException`: The range holds merged cells, or part of an array formula or a spill.
- `NotSupportedException`: The range holds a formula SharpCell cannot read (such as a link to another workbook).

<a id="tocsv-char"></a>
### ToCsv(char)

```csharp
public string ToCsv(char delimiter = ,)
```

The range as CSV text, as Excel's Save As CSV writes it: each cell as it shows (with its number format), fields holding the delimiter, a quote or a line break in quotes, quotes doubled, and each row ending in CRLF. Whole columns such as `A:C` end at the last row used. Formulas out of date are calculated first.

**Parameters**

- `delimiter`: What separates the fields; Excel uses `;` where the decimal separator is a comma.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The delimiter is a quote or a line break.

<a id="todatatable-bool"></a>
### ToDataTable(bool)

```csharp
public DataTable ToDataTable(bool headers = true)
```

The range as a `DataTable` named after the sheet, one row per row of the range. With `headers`, the first row names the columns (`ColumnN` for an empty one, a number added to a repeated one, as tables name them); otherwise they are `Column1`, `Column2` and so on. A column whose values are all numbers is `Double`, all shown as dates `DateTime`, all logical values `Boolean`, all text `String`; any other mix is `Object`, with errors as their text (`#N/A`). Empty cells are `DBNull`. Whole columns such as `A:C` end at the last row used. Formulas out of date are calculated first.

**Parameters**

- `headers`: Whether the first row holds the column names.

<a id="tostring"></a>
### ToString()

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

The address with the sheet name as a formula writes it, such as `Sheet1!A1:C10` or `'My Sheet'!B2`.

<a id="writecsv-textwriter-char"></a>
### WriteCsv(TextWriter, char)

```csharp
public void WriteCsv(TextWriter writer, char delimiter = ,)
```

Writes the range as CSV text, for a file or a stream; see [CellRange.ToCsv](SharpCell.CellRange.md#tocsv-char).

**Parameters**

- `writer`: Where to write, in the encoding it has.
- `delimiter`: What separates the fields.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The delimiter is a quote or a line break.

---

## Methods

<a id="array-cellvalue"></a>
### Array(CellValue[,])

```csharp

```

A rectangular array. The array is taken by reference and must not be mutated afterwards. Excel has no empty arrays, so both dimensions must be at least 1.

<a id="asarray"></a>
### AsArray()

```csharp
public CellValue[,] AsArray()
```

The array, rows first. Throws `InvalidOperationException` when [CellValue.Kind](SharpCell.CellValue.md#kind) is not [CellValueKind.Array](SharpCell.CellValueKind.md#array).

<a id="asboolean"></a>


The logical value. Throws `InvalidOperationException` when [CellValue.Kind](SharpCell.CellValue.md#kind) is not [CellValueKind.Boolean](SharpCell.CellValueKind.md#boolean).

<a id="asdatetime-datesystem"></a>
### AsDateTime(DateSystem)

```csharp
public DateTime AsDateTime(DateSystem system)
```

The number read as a date and time: Excel stores dates as serial days counted from the workbook's `system` ([Workbook.DateSystem](SharpCell.Workbook.md#datesystem)), the time of day as the fraction, here rounded to the millisecond. The result's kind is `DateTimeKind.Unspecified`, as Excel knows no time zones.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidOperationException`: [CellValue.Kind](SharpCell.CellValue.md#kind) is not [CellValueKind.Number](SharpCell.CellValueKind.md#number).
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The number is no date: negative, past 9999-12-31, or 60 in the 1900 system, which Excel shows as the non-existent 1900-02-29.

<a id="aserror"></a>
### AsError()

```csharp
public ErrorKind AsError()
```

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The date is before the date system starts: 1899-12-31 in the 1900 system, 1904-01-01 in the 1904 system.

<a id="lambda-lambdavalue"></a>
### Lambda(LambdaValue)

```csharp
public static CellValue Lambda(LambdaValue value)
```

A function value.

<a id="number-double"></a>
### Number(double)

```csharp
public static CellValue Number(double value)
```

A number. Excel has neither NaN, infinities nor negative zero: non-finite input becomes `#NUM!` and `-0` becomes `0`.

<a id="text-string"></a>
### Text(string)

```csharp
public static CellValue Text(string value)
```

A text value.

<a id="tostring"></a>
### ToString()

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

Formats the value the way it would be written as a formula literal.

## Operators

<a id="op-implicit-bool"></a>


A logical value, so `cell.Value = true` works.

<a id="op-implicit-double"></a>
### implicit operator CellValue(double)

```csharp
public static implicit operator CellValue(double value)
```

A number, so `cell.Value = 42` works.

<a id="op-implicit-string"></a>
### implicit operator CellValue(string)

```csharp
public static implicit operator CellValue(string value)
```

A text value, so `cell.Value = "text"` works.

<a id="op-inequality-cellvalue-cellvalue"></a>

```csharp
public static bool operator !=(CellValue left, CellValue right)
```

Whether the values differ, as [CellValue.Equals](SharpCell.CellValue.md#equals-cellvalue).

<a id="op-equality-cellvalue-cellvalue"></a>
### operator ==(CellValue, CellValue)

```csharp
public static bool operator ==(CellValue left, CellValue right)
```

Whether the values are equal, as [CellValue.Equals](SharpCell.CellValue.md#equals-cellvalue).

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.CellValueKind.md -->

# CellValueKind

```csharp
public enum CellValueKind
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

The kind of value a [CellValue](SharpCell.CellValue.md) holds.

## Values

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="empty"></a>`Empty` | 0 | An empty cell. Reads as 0, "" or FALSE depending on what the formula expects. |
| <a id="missing"></a>`Missing` | 1 | An argument left out of a function call, as in `IF(A1,,B1)`. |
| <a id="number"></a>`Number` | 2 | A number. Dates and times are numbers too: serial days since the workbook's date system epoch. |
| <a id="text"></a>`Text` | 3 | Text. |
| <a id="boolean"></a>`Boolean` | 4 | TRUE or FALSE. |
| <a id="error"></a>`Error` | 5 | An Excel error value such as `#DIV/0!`; errors are values, not exceptions. |
| <a id="array"></a>`Array` | 6 | A rectangular array, the result of a dynamic array formula or an array constant. |
| <a id="lambda"></a>`Lambda` | 7 | A function value created by `LAMBDA`. |

# CellVerticalAlignment

```csharp
public enum CellVerticalAlignment
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

Where a cell's text sits from top to bottom of the cell.

## Values

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="top"></a>`Top` | 0 | Against the top edge. |
| <a id="center"></a>`Center` | 1 | In the middle. |
| <a id="bottom"></a>`Bottom` | 2 | Against the bottom edge, Excel's default. |
| <a id="justify"></a>`Justify` | 3 | Lines spread to the top and bottom edges. |
| <a id="distributed"></a>`Distributed` | 4 | Lines spread evenly from top to bottom. |

# ColumnFilterType

```csharp
public enum ColumnFilterType
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

How a column of an [AutoFilter](SharpCell.AutoFilter.md) picks the rows it shows, as Excel's filter menu offers it.

## Values

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="values"></a>`Values` | 0 | Rows whose cell shows one of [ColumnFilter.Values](SharpCell.ColumnFilter.md#values) or [ColumnFilter.Dates](SharpCell.ColumnFilter.md#dates), or is blank when [ColumnFilter.Blanks](SharpCell.ColumnFilter.md#blanks): the menu's check boxes. |
| <a id="custom"></a>`Custom` | 1 | Rows whose cell meets one or two conditions: Text Filters and Number Filters > Custom Filter. |
| <a id="top"></a>`Top` | 2 | Rows with the highest numbers: Number Filters > Top 10. |
| <a id="bottom"></a>`Bottom` | 3 | Rows with the lowest numbers. |
| <a id="dynamic"></a>`Dynamic` | 4 | Rows above or below the average, or with dates in a period around today: [ColumnFilter.Dynamic](SharpCell.ColumnFilter.md#dynamic). |
| <a id="bycolor"></a>`ByColor` | 5 | Filter by Color (a fill, a font colour or an icon), read from a file. SharpCell keeps it when saving but cannot apply it, since cell colours from conditional formats are not worked out. |

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md -->

# ConditionalFormat

```csharp
public sealed class ConditionalFormat
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

A conditional format: which cells of its ranges it formats, and how. Make one with a factory such as [ConditionalFormat.CellValue](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#cellvalue-conditionaloperator-string-conditionalstyle-string), [ConditionalFormat.Expression](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#expression-string-conditionalstyle) or [ConditionalFormat.Top](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#top-int-conditionalstyle-bool), change it with `with` (`rule with { StopIfTrue = true }`), and add it with [Worksheet.AddConditionalFormat](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#addconditionalformat-string-conditionalformat). SharpCell works out which cells a rule applies to ([Cell.ConditionalFormats](SharpCell.Cell.md#conditionalformats)) and how a cell then looks ([Cell.DisplayStyle](SharpCell.Cell.md#displaystyle)).

## Properties

<a id="formula1"></a>
### Formula1

```csharp
public string? Formula1 { get; }
```

The formula of a [ConditionalFormatType.CellValue](SharpCell.ConditionalFormatType.md#cellvalue) or [ConditionalFormatType.Expression](SharpCell.ConditionalFormatType.md#expression) rule, starting with `=`, relative to the first cell of the rule's first range; null for other rules.

<a id="formula2"></a>
### Formula2

```csharp
public string? Formula2 { get; }
```

The second formula of a between rule; null for others.

<a id="operator"></a>
### Operator

```csharp
public ConditionalOperator Operator { get; }
```

How a [ConditionalFormatType.CellValue](SharpCell.ConditionalFormatType.md#cellvalue) rule compares; [ConditionalOperator.Between](SharpCell.ConditionalOperator.md#between) for other rules.

<a id="orequal"></a>
### OrEqual

```csharp
public bool OrEqual { get; }
```

Whether an above or below average rule also formats values equal to the average.

<a id="percent"></a>
### Percent

```csharp
public bool Percent { get; }
```

Whether [ConditionalFormat.Rank](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#rank) is a percentage.

<a id="period"></a>
### Period

```csharp
public TimePeriod Period { get; }
```

The period of a [ConditionalFormatType.TimePeriod](SharpCell.ConditionalFormatType.md#timeperiod) rule.

<a id="rank"></a>
### Rank

```csharp
public int Rank { get; }
```

How many values (or what percentage of them) a top or bottom rule formats; 0 for others.

<a id="standarddeviations"></a>
### StandardDeviations

```csharp
public int StandardDeviations { get; }
```

How many standard deviations above or below the average a value must be; 0 for the average itself.

<a id="stopiftrue"></a>
### StopIfTrue

```csharp
public bool StopIfTrue { get; init; }
```

Whether lower rules are skipped for a cell this rule applies to, as Excel's Stop If True does.

<a id="style"></a>
### Style

```csharp
public ConditionalStyle? Style { get; init; }
```

How matching cells look; null for colour scales, data bars and icon sets, which colour each cell themselves.

<a id="text"></a>
### Text

```csharp
public string? Text { get; }
```

The text a text rule looks for; null for others.

<a id="type"></a>
### Type

```csharp
public ConditionalFormatType Type { get; }
```

What the rule looks at.

## Methods

<a id="aboveaverage-conditionalstyle-bool-int"></a>
### AboveAverage(ConditionalStyle, bool, int)

```csharp
public static ConditionalFormat AboveAverage(ConditionalStyle style, bool orEqual = false, int standardDeviations = 0)
```

Numbers above the average of the ranges, or by `standardDeviations` standard deviations above it.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The standard deviations are outside 0 to 3, as in Excel.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is empty.

<a id="belowaverage-conditionalstyle-bool-int"></a>

```csharp
public static ConditionalFormat BelowAverage(ConditionalStyle style, bool orEqual = false, int standardDeviations = 0)
```

Numbers below the average of the ranges, or by `standardDeviations` standard deviations below it.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The standard deviations are outside 0 to 3, as in Excel.

<a id="blanks-conditionalstyle"></a>
### Blanks(ConditionalStyle)

```csharp
public static ConditionalFormat Blanks(ConditionalStyle style)
```

Empty cells and cells holding only spaces.

<a id="bottom-int-conditionalstyle-bool"></a>
### Bottom(int, ConditionalStyle, bool)

```csharp
public static ConditionalFormat Bottom(int rank, ConditionalStyle style, bool percent = false)
```

The `rank` lowest numbers of the ranges, or the lowest `rank` percent of them.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The rank is outside 1 to 1000, or a percentage outside 1 to 100.

<a id="cellvalue-conditionaloperator-string-conditionalstyle-string"></a>
### CellValue(ConditionalOperator, string, ConditionalStyle, string)

```csharp
public static ConditionalFormat CellValue(ConditionalOperator comparison, string formula1, ConditionalStyle style, string? formula2 = null)
```

Cells whose value compares with the formulas, such as greater than `=100` or between `=$B$1` and `=$B$2`.

**Parameters**

- `comparison`: How the value compares.
- `formula1`: The formula compared with, starting with `=`, relative to the range's first cell.
- `style`: How matching cells look.
- `formula2`: The second formula, for [ConditionalOperator.Between](SharpCell.ConditionalOperator.md#between) and [ConditionalOperator.NotBetween](SharpCell.ConditionalOperator.md#notbetween).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: A formula is missing or empty, or a second formula is given to a comparison that takes one.

<a id="containstext-string-conditionalstyle"></a>

```csharp
public static ConditionalFormat ContainsText(string text, ConditionalStyle style)
```

Cells whose text contains `text`, ignoring case.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is empty.



Cells whose text ends with `text`, ignoring case.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is empty.


Cells holding an error.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.ConditionalFormatType.md -->

# ConditionalFormatType

```csharp
public enum ConditionalFormatType
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

What a conditional format looks at, as Excel's New Formatting Rule dialog offers it.

## Values

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="cellvalue"></a>`CellValue` | 0 | The cell's value compared with formulas: Highlight Cells Rules > Greater Than and the others. |
| <a id="expression"></a>`Expression` | 1 | Cells for which a formula is true: Use a formula to determine which cells to format. |
| <a id="top"></a>`Top` | 2 | The highest values of the ranges: Top/Bottom Rules > Top 10 Items or Top 10%. |
| <a id="bottom"></a>`Bottom` | 3 | The lowest values of the ranges. |
| <a id="aboveaverage"></a>`AboveAverage` | 4 | Values above the average of the ranges. |
| <a id="belowaverage"></a>`BelowAverage` | 5 | Values below the average of the ranges. |
| <a id="duplicatevalues"></a>`DuplicateValues` | 6 | Values that appear more than once in the ranges. |
| <a id="uniquevalues"></a>`UniqueValues` | 7 | Values that appear once in the ranges. |
| <a id="containstext"></a>`ContainsText` | 8 | Text containing [ConditionalFormat.Text](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#text), ignoring case. |
| <a id="notcontainstext"></a>`NotContainsText` | 9 | Text not containing [ConditionalFormat.Text](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#text). |
| <a id="beginswith"></a>`BeginsWith` | 10 | Text beginning with [ConditionalFormat.Text](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#text). |
| <a id="endswith"></a>`EndsWith` | 11 | Text ending with [ConditionalFormat.Text](SharpCell.ConditionalFormat.md#text). |
| <a id="blanks"></a>`Blanks` | 12 | Empty cells, or cells holding only spaces. |
| <a id="noblanks"></a>`NoBlanks` | 13 | Cells that are not blank. |
| <a id="errors"></a>`Errors` | 14 | Cells holding an error. |
| <a id="noerrors"></a>`NoErrors` | 15 | Cells not holding an error. |
| <a id="timeperiod"></a>`TimePeriod` | 16 | Dates in a period around today: A Date Occurring. |
| <a id="colorscale"></a>`ColorScale` | 17 | A colour scale, read from a file; every number gets a colour of its own, which SharpCell does not work out. |
| <a id="databar"></a>`DataBar` | 18 | Data bars, read from a file. |
| <a id="iconset"></a>`IconSet` | 19 | An icon set, read from a file. |

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.ConditionalOperator.md -->

# ConditionalOperator

```csharp
public enum ConditionalOperator
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

How a [ConditionalFormatType.CellValue](SharpCell.ConditionalFormatType.md#cellvalue) rule compares the cell's value with its formulas.

## Values

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="between"></a>`Between` | 0 | From the first formula to the second, both included. |
| <a id="notbetween"></a>`NotBetween` | 1 | Less than the first formula or greater than the second. |
| <a id="equal"></a>`Equal` | 2 | Equal to the first formula; text ignoring case. |
| <a id="notequal"></a>`NotEqual` | 3 | Not equal to the first formula. |
| <a id="greaterthan"></a>`GreaterThan` | 4 | Greater than the first formula. |
| <a id="lessthan"></a>`LessThan` | 5 | Less than the first formula. |
| <a id="greaterthanorequal"></a>`GreaterThanOrEqual` | 6 | Greater than or equal to the first formula. |
| <a id="lessthanorequal"></a>`LessThanOrEqual` | 7 | Less than or equal to the first formula. |

---

# DataValidation

```csharp
public sealed class DataValidation
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

A data validation rule: what the cells of a range accept and the messages Excel shows for them. Set properties in an initializer, or start from [DataValidation.List](SharpCell.DataValidation.md#list-string), [DataValidation.ListFrom](SharpCell.DataValidation.md#listfrom-string) or [DataValidation.Custom](SharpCell.DataValidation.md#custom-string). SharpCell keeps the rule with the cells and saves it; it does not check values.

## Constructors

<a id="ctor"></a>
### DataValidation()

```csharp
public DataValidation()
```

A rule allowing any value; set properties in an initializer.

<a id="ctor-datavalidation"></a>

```csharp
public DataValidation(DataValidation source)
```

A copy of another rule, so a factory's rule can be changed in an initializer: `new DataValidation(DataValidation.List("Yes", "No")) { ErrorMessage = "Choose Yes or No." }`.

**Parameters**

- `source`: The rule to copy.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: The source is null.

## Properties

The first formula, with a leading `=` (added if missing) as [Cell.Formula](SharpCell.Cell.md#formula) takes it, or null: the low end or the value compared with, the list (`="Yes,No"` or `=$H$1:$H$5`) or the custom condition (`=A1>0`). Relative references are relative to the first cell of the rule's first range. It is parsed when the rule is added to a sheet.

# ErrorKind

```csharp
public enum ErrorKind
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

Excel error values. Numeric values match the codes returned by `ERROR.TYPE`.

## Values

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="null"></a>`Null` | 1 | `#NULL!`: the intersection of two ranges is empty. |
| <a id="div0"></a>`Div0` | 2 | `#DIV/0!`: division by zero. |
| <a id="value"></a>`Value` | 3 | `#VALUE!`: an argument has the wrong type. |
| <a id="ref"></a>`Ref` | 4 | `#REF!`: a reference is not valid. |
| <a id="name"></a>`Name` | 5 | `#NAME?`: an unknown function or name. |
| <a id="num"></a>`Num` | 6 | `#NUM!`: a number is out of range or a calculation does not converge. |
| <a id="na"></a>`NA` | 7 | `#N/A`: a value is not available, such as a lookup that found nothing. |
| <a id="spill"></a>`Spill` | 9 | `#SPILL!`: a dynamic array result cannot spill because cells are in the way. |
| <a id="calc"></a>`Calc` | 14 | `#CALC!`: the calculation cannot produce a result, such as an empty array. |

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.FunctionCollection.md -->

# FunctionCollection

```csharp
public sealed class FunctionCollection
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

The functions a workbook's formulas can call besides Excel's: add one with [FunctionCollection.Add](SharpCell.FunctionCollection.md#add-string-func-functionarguments-cellvalue-functionoptions), and formulas calling it by name (ignoring case) use it from the next calculation on.

## Properties

<a id="names"></a>
### Names

```csharp
public IReadOnlyCollection<string> Names { get; }
```

The names of the added functions, as they were added.

## Methods

<a id="add-string-func-functionarguments-cellvalue-functionoptions"></a>
### Add(string, Func<FunctionArguments, CellValue>, FunctionOptions)

```csharp
public void Add(string name, Func<FunctionArguments, CellValue> body, FunctionOptions? options = null)
```

Adds a function. Formulas that call the name, and were `#NAME?` so far, are calculated again by the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken). Calls written `_xll.NAME(...)` or `_xludf.NAME(...)`, as Excel stores calls of add-in functions in files, find it too.

**Parameters**

- `name`: Letters, digits, `.` and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`; not the name of a function SharpCell implements. A name Excel knows but SharpCell does not implement, such as `WEBSERVICE`, is allowed.
- `body`: Calculates the result from the arguments. It must not change the workbook, and it should read cells only through its arguments: cells it reads otherwise are not dependencies, so it is not calculated again when they change. An exception it throws makes the cell `#VALUE!` with a [DiagnosticKind.CustomFunctionFailure](SharpCell.DiagnosticKind.md#customfunctionfailure) diagnostic.
- `options`: Argument counts, which parameters are scalar, and whether the function is volatile; null for any number of arguments passed as they are.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The name is not a function name, is built in, or was added already; or the options are not consistent.

<a id="contains-string"></a>
### Contains(string)

```csharp
public bool Contains(string name)
```

Whether a function of that name was added, ignoring case.

<a id="remove-string"></a>
### Remove(string)

```csharp
public bool Remove(string name)
```

Removes a function. Formulas calling it become `#NAME?` at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Returns:** Whether a function of that name was there.

---

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.FunctionOptions.md -->

# FunctionOptions

```csharp
public sealed class FunctionOptions
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

How a function added through [Workbook.Functions](SharpCell.Workbook.md#functions) takes its arguments.

## Constructors

<a id="ctor"></a>
### FunctionOptions()

```csharp
public FunctionOptions()
```

Options for any number of arguments, all passed as they are, and a function that is not volatile.

## Properties

<a id="isvolatile"></a>
### IsVolatile

```csharp
public bool IsVolatile { get; init; }
```

Whether the function is calculated on every [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken), like `NOW`, instead of only when its arguments change.

<a id="maxarguments"></a>
### MaxArguments

```csharp
public int MaxArguments { get; init; }
```

The most arguments a call may have, up to 255 as in Excel; more make the call `#VALUE!`. Default 255.

<a id="minarguments"></a>
### MinArguments

```csharp
public int MinArguments { get; init; }
```

The fewest arguments a call may have; fewer make the call `#VALUE!`. Default 0.

<a id="scalarparameters"></a>
### ScalarParameters

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<int> ScalarParameters { get; init; }
```

The 0-based positions of scalar parameters. A scalar parameter receives one value: given a range or an array, the function is called once per element and the results spill, as with Excel's own functions such as `LEN(A1:A10)`. Other parameters receive the argument as it is: a range as an array of its values.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.Hyperlink.md -->

# Hyperlink

```csharp
public sealed class Hyperlink
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

A hyperlink on a cell: a web or e-mail address, a file, or a place in the workbook. The cell's value is what Excel shows; the link neither changes it nor applies the Hyperlink cell style.

## Constructors

<a id="ctor-string-string"></a>
### Hyperlink(string, string)

```csharp
public Hyperlink(string target, string? tooltip = null)
```

A link to `target`, with an optional tooltip.

**Parameters**

- `target`: A web or e-mail address or a file (`https://example.com`, `mailto:a@example.com`, `report.pdf`), or a place in the workbook written as Excel's HYPERLINK function takes it: `#Sheet2!A1`, `#'Q1 Sales'!A1` or `#MyName`.
- `tooltip`: Excel's ScreenTip, shown when the pointer rests on the cell; at most 255 characters, or null for none.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: The target is null.
- `ArgumentException`: The target is empty or only `#`, or the tooltip is longer than 255 characters.

## Properties

<a id="isinworkbook"></a>
### IsInWorkbook

```csharp
public bool IsInWorkbook { get; }
```

Whether the link goes to a place in this workbook, that is, the target starts with `#`.

<a id="target"></a>
### Target

```csharp
public string Target { get; }
```

Where the link goes, as given to the constructor.

An empty fragment is dropped when the link is saved: `https://example.com/#` reads back as `https://example.com/`.

<a id="tooltip"></a>
### Tooltip

```csharp
public string? Tooltip { get; }
```

The ScreenTip, or null for none.

## Methods

<a id="equals-hyperlink"></a>
### Equals(Hyperlink)

```csharp
public bool Equals(Hyperlink? other)
```

Whether the other link has the same target and tooltip, compared ordinally.

<a id="equals-object"></a>
### Equals(object)

```csharp
public override bool Equals(object? obj)
```

Whether `obj` is the same link.

<a id="gethashcode"></a>
### GetHashCode()

```csharp
public override int GetHashCode()
```

A hash code consistent with [Hyperlink.Equals](SharpCell.Hyperlink.md#equals-hyperlink).

<a id="tostring"></a>
### ToString()

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

The target.

---

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.IterationSettings.md -->

# IterationSettings

```csharp
public sealed class IterationSettings
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

Iterative calculation, Excel's "Enable iterative calculation": circular references are calculated over and over until they settle, instead of giving 0.

## Constructors

<a id="ctor-bool-int-double"></a>
### IterationSettings(bool, int, double)

```csharp
public IterationSettings(bool Enabled = false, int MaxIterations = 100, double MaxChange = 0.001)
```

Settings for iterative calculation; the defaults are Excel's, with iteration off.

**Parameters**

- `Enabled`: Whether circular references are calculated iteratively.
- `MaxIterations`: The most passes over a circular reference, 1 to 32,767.
- `MaxChange`: A circular reference has settled when no value of it changed by more than this in a pass; 0 or more.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: A limit is outside what Excel allows.

## Properties

<a id="enabled"></a>
### Enabled

```csharp
public bool Enabled { get; }
```

Whether circular references are calculated iteratively.

<a id="maxchange"></a>
### MaxChange

```csharp
public double MaxChange { get; }
```

A circular reference has settled when no value changed by more than this in a pass; 0.001 by default.

<a id="maxiterations"></a>
### MaxIterations

```csharp
public int MaxIterations { get; }
```

The most passes over a circular reference; 100 by default.

## Methods

<a id="equals-iterationsettings"></a>
### Equals(IterationSettings)

```csharp
public bool Equals(IterationSettings? other)
```

Whether the other settings are the same.

<a id="equals-object"></a>
### Equals(object)

```csharp
public override bool Equals(object? obj)
```

Whether `obj` is the same settings.

<a id="gethashcode"></a>
### GetHashCode()

```csharp
public override int GetHashCode()
```

A hash code consistent with [IterationSettings.Equals](SharpCell.IterationSettings.md#equals-iterationsettings).

<a id="tostring"></a>
### ToString()

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

The settings as text, such as `Enabled, 100 iterations, change 0.001`.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.RecalculationResult.md -->

# RecalculationResult

```csharp
public sealed class RecalculationResult
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

What one [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken) did.

## Properties

<a id="changedcells"></a>
### ChangedCells

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<Cell> ChangedCells { get; }
```

The cells whose values calculation changed since the previous [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken) (or since the workbook was loaded or cloned): formula cells, and cells a spill filled, changed or left (those are now empty). Cells you changed yourself are not included, nor cells that changed and changed back. In the order of their sheets in the workbook, then by row and column.

## Values

# Workbook

```csharp
public sealed class Workbook
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

A workbook: sheets, defined names and calculation settings. Not thread-safe; separate workbooks can be used from different threads.

## Constructors

```csharp
public Workbook()
```

An empty workbook with no sheets, the invariant culture and the 1900 date system.

## Properties


Culture for text-to-number conversion, number-to-text conversion and text ordering. The process culture is never used. Defaults to the invariant culture.

<a id="datesystem"></a>

```csharp

```

Whether serial dates count from 1900 or from 1904, as set in the file.

<a id="defaultstyle"></a>
### DefaultStyle

```csharp
public CellStyle DefaultStyle { get; set; }
```

The style of every cell without one of its own: the Normal style of a file read with SharpCell.Xlsx, [CellStyle.Default](SharpCell.CellStyle.md#default) for a new workbook.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: The style is null.

<a id="definednames"></a>
### DefinedNames

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<DefinedName> DefinedNames { get; }
```

The defined names, workbook-wide and sheet-scoped, in the order they were first defined: a snapshot that later definitions do not change.

<a id="diagnostics"></a>
### Diagnostics

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<CalculationDiagnostic> Diagnostics { get; }
```

Current calculation problems: circular references and failing functions. An entry of a cell disappears when the cell is edited or calculated without the problem; entries from [Workbook.Evaluate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#evaluate-string) last until the next call of it.

<a id="functions"></a>
### Functions

```csharp
public FunctionCollection Functions { get; }
```

Functions of your own that formulas of this workbook can call, besides Excel's.

<a id="isstructureprotected"></a>
### IsStructureProtected

```csharp
public bool IsStructureProtected { get; }
```

Whether the workbook's structure is locked: Excel then refuses adding, deleting, renaming, moving and hiding sheets.

<a id="iswindowsprotected"></a>
### IsWindowsProtected

```csharp
public bool IsWindowsProtected { get; }
```

Whether the workbook's windows are locked: Excel then refuses moving and resizing them.

<a id="iteration"></a>
### Iteration

```csharp
public IterationSettings Iteration { get; set; }
```

Iterative calculation of circular references, off by default as in Excel; the .xlsx reader sets it from the file. Changing it calculates every formula again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

<a id="sheets"></a>
### Sheets

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<Worksheet> Sheets { get; }
```

The sheets in order.

<a id="tables"></a>
### Tables

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<Table> Tables { get; }
```

The tables of all sheets, in the order they were added.

<a id="item-string"></a>
### this[string]

```csharp
public Worksheet this[string name] { get; }
```

Gets a sheet by name, ignoring case.

## Methods

<a id="addsheet-string"></a>
### AddSheet(string)

```csharp
public Worksheet AddSheet(string name)
```

Adds a sheet at the end.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The name is not a valid sheet name, or a sheet with that name exists.

<a id="clone"></a>
### Clone()

```csharp
public Workbook Clone()
```

An independent copy: sheets, cells and their calculated values, formulas still out of date, spills, diagnostics, defined names, tables, hidden rows, settings and custom functions (the same delegates), and the file it was read from, so `XlsxWriter` can save the copy too. Nothing is calculated again. Parsed formulas and the file's bytes are shared, not copied.

Cloning only reads this workbook, so several threads may clone it at the same time as long as nothing changes or calculates it meanwhile: a service can load a template once and clone it for each request. Like any workbook, each copy is for one thread at a time.

**Returns:** The copy; [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken) on it reports changes from this point on only.

<a id="definename-string-string-worksheet"></a>
### DefineName(string, string, Worksheet)

```csharp
public void DefineName(string name, string formula, Worksheet? scope = null)
```

Defines or replaces a name. A name with a `scope` is visible only on that sheet.

<a id="evaluate-string"></a>
### Evaluate(string)

```csharp
public CellValue Evaluate(string formula)
```

Evaluates a formula that belongs to no cell, as if it were in cell A1 of the first sheet. Out-of-date cells it reads are calculated first. References without a sheet are `#REF!` when the workbook has no sheets. The formula is in no table and has no row of its own: a table reference without a table name is `#REF!` and `[#This Row]` is `#VALUE!`.

<a id="evaluate-string-cancellationtoken"></a>
### Evaluate(string, CancellationToken)

```csharp
public CellValue Evaluate(string formula, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
```

Evaluates a formula that belongs to no cell, as if it were in cell A1 of the first sheet. Out-of-date cells it reads are calculated first. References without a sheet are `#REF!` when the workbook has no sheets. The formula is in no table and has no row of its own: a table reference without a table name is `#REF!` and `[#This Row]` is `#VALUE!`.

**Exceptions**

- `OperationCanceledException`: The token was cancelled.

<a id="movesheet-worksheet-int"></a>
### MoveSheet(Worksheet, int)

```csharp
public void MoveSheet(Worksheet sheet, int index)
```

Moves a sheet to another place in the order, as dragging its tab in Excel does. Formulas do not change, but a reference through several sheets (`Sheet1:Sheet3!A1`) takes in the sheets now between its ends, so every formula is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Parameters**

- `sheet`: A sheet of this workbook.
- `index`: Its new place in [Workbook.Sheets](SharpCell.Workbook.md#sheets), from 0.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The sheet is not in this workbook.
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The index is not a place in [Workbook.Sheets](SharpCell.Workbook.md#sheets).

<a id="protect-string-bool-bool"></a>
### Protect(string, bool, bool)

```csharp
public void Protect(string? password = null, bool structure = true, bool windows = false)
```

Protects the workbook as Excel's Protect Workbook does. SharpCell itself does not enforce protection: code may still add, remove and rename sheets, as Excel's object model may with the password. Protecting a protected workbook replaces its locks and password.

**Parameters**

- `password`: The password Excel asks for to unprotect the workbook, or null (or empty) for none. Only its hash is kept, made as Excel makes it (SHA-512, a random salt, 100,000 spins); it cannot be read back.
- `structure`: Whether to lock the structure: adding, deleting, renaming, moving and hiding sheets.
- `windows`: Whether to lock the windows' position and size.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: Both `structure` and `windows` are false.

<a id="recalculate-cancellationtoken"></a>
### Recalculate(CancellationToken)

```csharp
public RecalculationResult Recalculate(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
```

Calculates every formula that is out of date: those whose inputs changed since the last calculation and those using volatile functions (NOW, RAND).

**Returns:** The cells whose values calculation changed since the previous call, including what [Workbook.Evaluate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#evaluate-string) calculated in between.

**Exceptions**

- `OperationCanceledException`: The token was cancelled; finished cells keep their new values, and their changes are reported by the next call.

<a id="removesheet-worksheet"></a>
### RemoveSheet(Worksheet)

```csharp
public void RemoveSheet(Worksheet sheet)
```

Removes a sheet, as Excel's Delete Sheet does. References to it become `#REF!` (`=Sheet2!A1` becomes `=#REF!A1`) in formulas of every other sheet, defined names, data validation and conditional formats; a reference through several sheets that starts or ends at it keeps the sheets left between its ends. Names local to the sheet and its tables go with it, and references to those tables become `#REF!`. Every formula is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken). The sheet object can still be read, but not changed ([Worksheet.IsRemoved](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#isremoved)).

**Parameters**

- `sheet`: A sheet of this workbook.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The sheet is not in this workbook.
- `InvalidOperationException`: It is the last visible sheet while hidden ones remain: a workbook keeps at least one visible sheet.
- `NotSupportedException`: A formula naming the sheet cannot be read by SharpCell (such as a link to another workbook), so it could not be broken as Excel breaks it.

<a id="trygetsheet-string-worksheet"></a>
### TryGetSheet(string, Worksheet)

```csharp
public bool TryGetSheet(string name, out Worksheet? sheet)
```

Finds a sheet by name, ignoring case.

**Returns:** Whether the sheet exists.

<a id="trygettable-string-table"></a>
### TryGetTable(string, Table)

```csharp
public bool TryGetTable(string name, out Table? table)
```

Finds a table by name, ignoring case.

**Returns:** Whether the table exists.

<a id="unprotect"></a>
### Unprotect()

```csharp
public void Unprotect()
```

Removes the workbook's protection and its password, as Excel's Unprotect Workbook does once the password is given.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.Worksheet.md -->

# Worksheet

```csharp
public sealed class Worksheet
```

Namespace `SharpCell` · package `SharpCell`

A sheet of a [Workbook](SharpCell.Workbook.md). Reading a cell that was never set costs nothing: a [Cell](SharpCell.Cell.md) is a handle, and storage is allocated only when a value or formula is set.

## Properties

<a id="autofilter"></a>
### AutoFilter

```csharp
public AutoFilter? AutoFilter { get; }
```

The sheet's filter, Excel's Data > Filter; null when it has none. Tables have filters of their own, which this is not.

<a id="cells"></a>
### Cells

```csharp
public IEnumerable<Cell> Cells { get; }
```

The cells of the sheet that hold something (a constant, a formula or a value spilled into them), row by row and left to right. Values and formulas may be changed while enumerating; adding or removing a cell makes the next step throw `InvalidOperationException`.

<a id="columnpagebreaks"></a>
### ColumnPageBreaks

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<int> ColumnPageBreaks { get; }
```

The columns that start a new printed page, in order.

<a id="conditionalformats"></a>
### ConditionalFormats

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<(IReadOnlyList<CellRange>, ConditionalFormat)> ConditionalFormats { get; }
```

The conditional formats in priority order, highest first, each with its ranges. The formulas of a rule are relative to the first cell of its first range.

<a id="defaultcolumnwidth"></a>
### DefaultColumnWidth

```csharp
public double? DefaultColumnWidth { get; set; }
```

The width of columns without one of their own, as .xlsx files store it: in characters of the widest digit of the workbook's default font, padding included. Excel's standard 8.43 characters of Calibri 11 are 9.140625 here. Null when not given; Excel then uses 8 characters.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The width is outside 0 to 255.

<a id="defaultrowheight"></a>
### DefaultRowHeight

```csharp
public double? DefaultRowHeight { get; set; }
```

The height of rows without one of their own, in points. Null when not given; Excel then fits it to the default font, 15 points for Calibri 11.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The height is outside 0 to 409.

<a id="filtermode"></a>
### FilterMode

```csharp
public bool FilterMode { get; set; }
```

Whether the sheet has a filter with criteria, like `Worksheet.FilterMode` in Excel. Excel then treats every hidden row of the sheet as filtered out, so SUBTOTAL with codes 1–11 skips them as well; without a filter it counts them. AGGREGATE does not look at it.

<a id="frozencolumns"></a>
### FrozenColumns

```csharp
public int FrozenColumns { get; set; }
```

How many columns on the left stay in place while the rest scrolls; 0 for none.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The count is negative or leaves no column to scroll.

<a id="frozenrows"></a>
### FrozenRows

```csharp
public int FrozenRows { get; set; }
```

How many rows at the top stay in place while the rest scrolls, as Excel's Freeze Panes keeps them; 0 for none.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The count is negative or leaves no row to scroll.

<a id="isremoved"></a>
### IsRemoved

```csharp

```

Whether [Workbook.RemoveSheet](SharpCell.Workbook.md#removesheet-worksheet) took the sheet out of its workbook; it can then be read but not changed.

<a id="mergedareas"></a>

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<CellRange> MergedAreas { get; }
```

The merged areas, in the order they were merged.

<a id="name"></a>
### Name

```csharp
public string Name { get; set; }
```

The sheet name. Renaming a sheet renames it in every formula that refers to it, as Excel does: in cells of every sheet, defined names, data validation and conditional formats. Text inside INDIRECT and hyperlinks into the sheet keep the old name, as in Excel. Every formula is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The name is not a valid sheet name, or another sheet has it, ignoring case.
- `NotSupportedException`: A formula naming the sheet cannot be read by SharpCell (such as a link to another workbook), so it could not follow the new name.
- `InvalidOperationException`: The sheet was removed from its workbook.

The cells with a note, row by row and left to right, with their notes.

<a id="pagemargins"></a>

```csharp
public PageMargins PageMargins { get; set; }
```

The margins of the printed pages; [PageMargins.Normal](SharpCell.PageMargins.md#normal) unless set otherwise.

<a id="pageorientation"></a>

```csharp
public PageOrientation PageOrientation { get; set; }
```

**Exceptions**

<a id="printarea"></a>
### PrintArea

```csharp
public string? PrintArea { get; set; }
```

The cells that print, as Excel's Print Area sets them: one range such as `A1:F40`, or several separated by commas, each printed on pages of its own. Null prints every cell that holds something, which is also what setting null gives. Read without `$` signs; written with or without them. The ranges move with their cells when rows, columns or cells are inserted or deleted, as the defined name Excel keeps them in does.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is not A1 ranges of this sheet separated by commas.

<a id="printtitlecolumns"></a>
### PrintTitleColumns

```csharp
public string? PrintTitleColumns { get; set; }
```

The columns printed at the left of every page: `A:A` or `A:B`. Null for none. They move with their columns when columns are inserted or deleted.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is not a span of whole columns such as `A:B`.

<a id="printtitlerows"></a>
### PrintTitleRows

```csharp
public string? PrintTitleRows { get; set; }
```

The rows printed at the top of every page, as Excel's Print Titles sets them: `1:1` or `1:3`. Null for none. They move with their rows when rows are inserted or deleted.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is not a span of whole rows such as `1:2`.

The data validation rules, one entry per range: a rule over several ranges has an entry for each, in order. The formulas of a rule are relative to the first cell of its first range.

## Methods

<a id="addcolumnpagebreak-int"></a>
### AddColumnPageBreak(int)

```csharp
public void AddColumnPageBreak(int column)
```

Starts a new printed page at a column: a page break left of it.

**Parameters**

- `column`: The first column of the new page, from 2 (B).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The column is not on the sheet or is column A.

<a id="addconditionalformat-string-conditionalformat"></a>
### AddConditionalFormat(string, ConditionalFormat)

```csharp
public void AddConditionalFormat(string range, ConditionalFormat format)
```

Adds a conditional format to a range, below the rules the sheet has: where several apply to a cell, those added earlier win. Formulas are relative to the range's top-left cell; for several ranges, to the first one's.

**Parameters**

- `range`: The cells, such as `B2:B10`, or several ranges separated by spaces, such as `B2:B10 D2:D10`.
- `format`: The rule.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: The format is null.
- `ArgumentException`: The range is not an A1 range, or the format is one only read from files (a colour scale, data bars or an icon set).
- `FormulaParseException`: A formula cannot be parsed; nothing is added.

<a id="addrowpagebreak-int"></a>
### AddRowPageBreak(int)

```csharp
public void AddRowPageBreak(int row)
```

Starts a new printed page at a row: a page break above it. Breaks move with their rows.

**Parameters**

- `row`: The first row of the new page, from 2.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The row is not on the sheet or is row 1.

<a id="addtable-string-string-bool-bool"></a>
### AddTable(string, string, bool, bool)

```csharp
public Table AddTable(string name, string range, bool hasHeaderRow = true, bool hasTotalsRow = false)
```

Makes a range a table that formulas can refer to by name, as in `Sales[Units]`. Column names come from the header row as it is now: a cell's value as text (a formula's too), `ColumnN` for an empty cell or an error (N counts from the table's first column), and a number added to a repeated name (`Units2`). Without a header row the columns are `Column1`, `Column2` and so on. Changing a header cell later does not rename its column.

**Parameters**

- `name`: The table name; tables and defined names share one set of names, ignoring case.
- `range`: An A1 range on this sheet, such as `A1:D10`, including the header and totals rows; a single cell such as `A1` is a one-cell table without a header row.
- `hasHeaderRow`: Whether the first row holds the column names.
- `hasTotalsRow`: Whether the last row holds totals.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The name is not valid or is taken, the range is not an area, overlaps another table or has no row for data.

<a id="addvalidation-string-datavalidation"></a>
### AddValidation(string, DataValidation)

```csharp
public void AddValidation(string range, DataValidation validation)
```

Adds a data validation rule to a range. Cells of the range leave the rules they had, as in Excel, where a cell has one rule. The formulas are relative to the range's top-left cell; for several ranges, to the first one's.

**Parameters**

- `range`: The cells, such as `B2:B10`, or several ranges separated by spaces as Excel writes them, such as `B2:B10 D2:D10`.
- `validation`: The rule.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: The validation is null.
- `ArgumentException`: The range is not an A1 range; or a rule other than [ValidationType.Any](SharpCell.ValidationType.md#any) has no [DataValidation.Formula1](SharpCell.DataValidation.md#formula1); or a comparing rule (whole number, decimal, date, time, text length) with [ValidationOperator.Between](SharpCell.ValidationOperator.md#between) or [ValidationOperator.NotBetween](SharpCell.ValidationOperator.md#notbetween) has no [DataValidation.Formula2](SharpCell.DataValidation.md#formula2).
- `FormulaParseException`: A formula cannot be parsed; nothing is added.
- `NotSupportedException`: The range takes the first cell of a rule read from a file whose formula SharpCell cannot read, so the formula could not be moved to the rule's new first cell.

<a id="clearconditionalformats"></a>
### ClearConditionalFormats()

```csharp
public void ClearConditionalFormats()
```

Removes every conditional format of the sheet, as Excel's Clear Rules from Entire Sheet does.

<a id="clearconditionalformats-string"></a>
### ClearConditionalFormats(string)

```csharp
public void ClearConditionalFormats(string range)
```

Takes the cells of a range out of every conditional format, as Excel's Clear Rules from Selected Cells does; a rule left without cells is removed.

**Parameters**

- `range`: The cells, such as `A1:Z100`, or several ranges separated by spaces.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The range is not an A1 range.
- `NotSupportedException`: The range takes the first cell of a rule read from a file whose formula SharpCell cannot read, so the formula could not be moved to the rule's new first cell.

<a id="clearvalidation-string"></a>
### ClearValidation(string)

```csharp
public void ClearValidation(string range)
```

Takes the cells of a range out of every data validation rule; a rule left without cells is removed. A rule that loses its first cell keeps its formulas relative to its new first cell, so every remaining cell is checked as before.

**Parameters**

- `range`: The cells, such as `A1:Z100`, or several ranges separated by spaces.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The range is not an A1 range.
- `NotSupportedException`: The range takes the first cell of a rule read from a file whose formula SharpCell cannot read, so the formula could not be moved to the rule's new first cell.

<a id="columnwidth-int"></a>
### ColumnWidth(int)

```csharp
public double? ColumnWidth(int column)
```

A column's own width, in the units of [Worksheet.DefaultColumnWidth](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#defaultcolumnwidth); null when it has none.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The column is outside the sheet.

<a id="deletecolumns-int-int"></a>
### DeleteColumns(int, int)

```csharp
public void DeleteColumns(int column, int count = 1)
```

Deletes columns; see [Worksheet.DeleteRows](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#deleterows-int-int).

**Parameters**

- `column`: The first column to delete, from 1 (A is 1).
- `count`: How many columns to delete.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The columns are not all on the sheet.
- `InvalidOperationException`: The columns hold part of an array formula.
- `NotSupportedException`: The columns are some but not all of a table's columns, or a formula on this sheet, or one naming it, cannot be read by SharpCell.

<a id="deleterows-int-int"></a>
### DeleteRows(int, int)

```csharp
public void DeleteRows(int row, int count = 1)
```

Deletes rows, as Excel's Delete Sheet Rows does: cells below move up. A reference to a deleted cell becomes `#REF!`, a range that loses some of its rows shrinks, and a table whose rows are all deleted is removed. Every formula is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Parameters**

- `row`: The first row to delete, from 1.
- `count`: How many rows to delete.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The rows are not all on the sheet.
- `InvalidOperationException`: The rows hold part of an array formula, or a table's header or totals row or all its data rows without the whole table.
- `NotSupportedException`: A formula on this sheet, or one naming it, cannot be read by SharpCell.

<a id="insertcolumns-int-int"></a>
### InsertColumns(int, int)

```csharp
public void InsertColumns(int column, int count = 1)
```

Inserts empty columns before `column`; see [Worksheet.InsertRows](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#insertrows-int-int).

**Parameters**

- `column`: The column the new columns take the place of, from 1 (A is 1).
- `count`: How many columns to insert.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The columns would not fit on the sheet.
- `InvalidOperationException`: Content would be pushed past the last column, or the columns would split an array formula.
- `NotSupportedException`: The columns would be inserted inside a table, or a formula on this sheet, or one naming it, cannot be read by SharpCell.

<a id="insertrows-int-int"></a>
### InsertRows(int, int)

```csharp
public void InsertRows(int row, int count = 1)
```

Inserts empty rows before `row`, as Excel's Insert Sheet Rows does. Cells, styles, row heights, hidden rows, merged cells, tables and data validation below move down, and every reference to them follows: in formulas of every sheet, in defined names and in data validation. A range that spans the new rows grows; a table, merged area or validated range they are inserted into grows. Every formula is calculated again at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Parameters**

- `row`: The row the new rows take the place of, from 1.
- `count`: How many rows to insert.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The rows would not fit on the sheet.
- `InvalidOperationException`: Content would be pushed past the last row, or the rows would split an array formula (Ctrl+Shift+Enter).
- `NotSupportedException`: A formula on this sheet, or one naming it, cannot be read by SharpCell (such as a link to another workbook), so its references could not follow.

<a id="iscolumnhidden-int"></a>
### IsColumnHidden(int)

```csharp
public bool IsColumnHidden(int column)
```

Whether a column is hidden.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The column is outside the sheet.

<a id="isrowhidden-int"></a>
### IsRowHidden(int)

```csharp
public bool IsRowHidden(int row)
```

Whether a row is hidden.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The row is outside the sheet.

<a id="loadcsv-string-textreader-char-bool"></a>
### LoadCsv(string, TextReader, char, bool)

```csharp
public CellRange LoadCsv(string topLeft, TextReader reader, char delimiter = ,, bool formulas = false)
```

Writes CSV text into the sheet starting at a cell, as Excel opens a .csv file: each field is read as if typed into its cell (see [Cell.Input](SharpCell.Cell.md#input)), so numbers, percentages, dates and logical values in the workbook's culture become those values, with a format taken from how they were written. Fields may be quoted, with quotes doubled and line breaks inside; rows end in CRLF, LF or CR. An empty field clears its cell. A field starting with `=` stays text unless `formulas` is set, since a file from elsewhere could hide formulas in it. Nothing is written unless all of it fits on the sheet.

**Parameters**

- `topLeft`: The cell of the first field, such as `A1`.
- `reader`: The CSV text.
- `delimiter`: What separates the fields; Excel uses `;` where the decimal separator is a comma.
- `formulas`: Whether a field starting with `=` is a formula, as Excel reads it.

**Returns:** The range written: as many rows as the text has, as wide as its widest row.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The address is not a cell, or the delimiter is a quote or a line break.
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The rows or fields run past the sheet's edge.
- `FormulaParseException`: With `formulas`, a field starting with `=` is not a formula.

<a id="loaddatatable-string-datatable-bool"></a>
### LoadDataTable(string, DataTable, bool)

```csharp
public CellRange LoadDataTable(string topLeft, DataTable table, bool headers = true)
```

Writes the rows of a `DataTable` starting at a cell, optionally under a header row of its column names, and returns the range written. Nothing is written unless every value could be converted. `DBNull` is an empty cell; other values are converted as [`Worksheet.LoadRows<T>`](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#loadrows-string-ienumerable-t-string-func-t-object) does.

**Parameters**

- `topLeft`: The cell of the first header (or of the first value without headers), such as `B2`.
- `table`: The table to write; it needs at least one column.
- `headers`: `true` to write the column names as a header row first.

**Returns:** The range written, header row included.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: An argument is null.
- `ArgumentException`: The table has no columns, the address is not a cell, or a value cannot be stored (NaN, infinity).
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The data runs past the last row or column, or a date is before the date system starts.

<a id="loadrows-string-ienumerable-t-string-func-t-object"></a>
### LoadRows<T>(string, IEnumerable<T>, (string, Func<T, object>)[])

```csharp
public CellRange LoadRows<T>(string topLeft, IEnumerable<T> rows, params (string Header, Func<T, object?> Value)[] columns)
```

Writes a header row and then one row per item of a collection, starting at a cell, and returns the range written (the header row included). The collection is enumerated once and nothing is written unless every value could be converted. Columns are lambdas, so no reflection is needed.

Values are converted like this:

- `null` and `DBNull` are empty and clear the cell; a [CellValue](SharpCell.CellValue.md) is stored as it is.
- A `String` or `Char` is text, never a formula: `"=1+1"` stays text.
- A `Boolean` is a logical value.
- Every integer type, `Single`, `Double` and `Decimal` is a number; NaN and infinities are rejected.
- A `DateTime` is a date serial in the workbook's date system, shown in the culture's short date and, with a time of day, hours and minutes. `DateOnly` is a date at midnight; `DateTimeOffset` is the clock time it states.
- A `TimeOnly` is a fraction of a day with a time format; a `TimeSpan` is a number of days shown as `[h]:mm:ss`.
- An enum is its name; anything else is its `IFormattable` text in the workbook's culture, or its `ToString()`.

Number cells keep the format they had; date and time cells take a format.

**Parameters**

- `topLeft`: The cell of the first header, such as `B2`.
- `rows`: The items; one row each.
- `columns`: The header of each column and how to get its value from an item.

**Returns:** The range written, header row included.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: An argument or a header is null.
- `ArgumentException`: There are no columns, the address is not a cell, or a value cannot be stored (NaN, infinity).
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The data runs past the last row or column, or a date is before the date system starts.

<a id="merge-string"></a>
### Merge(string)

```csharp
public void Merge(string address)
```

Merges a range of at least two cells into one, as Excel shows it: the top-left cell covers the range. The values of the other cells are kept; Excel's Merge command would clear them.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The address is not a range of two cells or more, or it overlaps a merged area.

<a id="protect-string-sheetprotection"></a>
### Protect(string, SheetProtection)

```csharp
public void Protect(string? password = null, SheetProtection? allow = null)
```

Protects the sheet as Excel's Protect Sheet does: Excel then refuses changes to locked cells and allows only the actions `allow` names. SharpCell itself does not enforce protection: code may still change the sheet, as Excel's object model may with the password. Protecting a protected sheet replaces its protection and password.

**Parameters**

- `password`: The password Excel asks for to unprotect the sheet, or null (or empty) for none. Only its hash is kept, made as Excel makes it (SHA-512, a random salt, 100,000 spins); it cannot be read back.
- `allow`: What users may still do; null for Excel's defaults, selecting cells only.

<a id="range-string"></a>
### Range(string)

```csharp
public CellRange Range(string address)
```

A range of this sheet by A1 address: `A1:C10`, `B2`, whole columns `A:B` or whole rows `2:3`.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is not such an address; a sheet name is not allowed.

<a id="removeautofilter"></a>
### RemoveAutoFilter()

```csharp
public void RemoveAutoFilter()
```

Turns the sheet's filter off, as clicking Excel's Filter again does: the rows it hid show, and the sheet is no longer in [Worksheet.FilterMode](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#filtermode). Nothing happens without a filter.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidOperationException`: The sheet was removed.

<a id="removecolumnpagebreak-int"></a>
### RemoveColumnPageBreak(int)

```csharp
public void RemoveColumnPageBreak(int column)
```

Removes the page break left of a column, if there is one.

**Parameters**

- `column`: The column.

<a id="removerowpagebreak-int"></a>
### RemoveRowPageBreak(int)


Removes the page break above a row, if there is one.

**Parameters**

- `row`: The row.

<a id="rowheight-int"></a>
### RowHeight(int)

```csharp
public double? RowHeight(int row)
```

A row's own height in points; null when it has none.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The row is outside the sheet.

<a id="setautofilter-string"></a>
### SetAutoFilter(string)

```csharp
public AutoFilter SetAutoFilter(string range)
```

Turns on Excel's filter for a range, its first row holding the buttons, and returns it to filter columns with. A filter the sheet had is removed first, showing the rows it hid.

**Parameters**

- `range`: An A1 range on this sheet with at least two rows, such as `A1:D20`; whole columns such as `A:D` are filtered down to the last row with something in it.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The text is not such a range, or the range overlaps a table.
- `InvalidOperationException`: The sheet was removed.

<a id="setcolumnhidden-int-bool"></a>

Hides or shows a column. Unlike hidden rows, hidden columns change no result, as in Excel.

<a id="setcolumnwidth-int-double"></a>

<a id="setrowhidden-int-bool"></a>
### SetRowHidden(int, bool)

```csharp
public void SetRowHidden(int row, bool hidden)
```

Hides or shows a row. SUBTOTAL with codes 101–111 and AGGREGATE with options 1, 3, 5 and 7 skip hidden rows; see [Worksheet.FilterMode](SharpCell.Worksheet.md#filtermode) for SUBTOTAL 1–11. Like any change, it shows at the next [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The row is outside the sheet.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.Xlsx.XlsxReader.md -->

# XlsxReader

```csharp
public static class XlsxReader
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Xlsx` · package `SharpCell.Xlsx`

Reads .xlsx workbooks: sheets, values, formulas with the results Excel cached, defined names, tables, hidden rows, whether a sheet is filtered, the date system, number formats, cell styles, column widths, row heights, merged cells, frozen panes and gridlines, from .xlsx and macro-enabled .xlsm files. Charts, pivot tables and macros are not read (a save keeps them; macros never run).

Every formula is out of date after loading: [Cell.Value](SharpCell.Cell.md#value) shows the value cached in the file until [Workbook.Recalculate](SharpCell.Workbook.md#recalculate-cancellationtoken) calculates it. A formula SharpCell cannot parse (for example a link to another workbook) does not fail the load; once calculated it is `#NAME?` and listed in [Workbook.Diagnostics](SharpCell.Workbook.md#diagnostics).

The workbook keeps the file's bytes in memory, so [XlsxWriter](SharpCell.Xlsx.XlsxWriter.md) can write changes into the same file.

## Methods

<a id="load-stream"></a>
### Load(Stream)

```csharp
public static Workbook Load(Stream stream)
```

Reads a workbook from a stream, which is left open.

**Parameters**

- `stream`: The .xlsx content; it need not be seekable.

**Returns:** The workbook, with the results Excel saved until it is recalculated.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidDataException`: The file is not a well-formed .xlsx workbook.
- `NotSupportedException`: The file is .xls, .xlsb or encrypted.

<a id="load-string"></a>
### Load(string)

```csharp
public static Workbook Load(string path)
```

Reads a workbook from a file.

**Parameters**

- `path`: Path of the .xlsx file.

**Returns:** The workbook, with the results Excel saved until it is recalculated.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidDataException`: The file is not a well-formed .xlsx workbook.
- `NotSupportedException`: The file is .xls, .xlsb or encrypted.

---

# XlsxWriteException

```csharp
public sealed class XlsxWriteException : InvalidOperationException
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Xlsx` · package `SharpCell.Xlsx`

A workbook was not saved because SharpCell could not calculate some of its formulas; see [XlsxWriteOptions.KeepUncalculated](SharpCell.Xlsx.XlsxWriteOptions.md#keepuncalculated).

### Problems

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<CalculationDiagnostic> Problems { get; }
```

The formula cells that could not be calculated, with the reason for each.
